SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. S. B REGISTRY

REPORT

Subject Re matters noted in the sale of cheap rice by 690 Chekiang Road and
84 Amoy Road rice-shops.

Made by S.I. Shao Kwang Liang. Forwarded by Officer i/c Louza.

FILE
21.10.40

Sir,

I beg to report that, between 1 pm. and 5 pm. on
5-10-40; the undersigned was on duty with C.P.C.s 77, 79
and 427 at 690 Chekiang Road and 84 Amoy Road rice-shops
looking after both shops re the sale of cheap rice.

At 1 pm. 5-10-40, the former of the above-
mentioned shops commenced selling the coupons with which
rice could be obtained from the latter shop. It is
understood that 2400 coupons are to be sold everyday.

At about 2.30 pm., the former shop declared that
all coupons had been sold out which declaration the
undersigned doubted, as this job required a more lengthy
period of time.

At about 4.30 pm., the latter shop finished
issuing rice and no more persons were seen coming for
same. The undersigned then checked the amount of
coupons collected with the assistance of the above-
mentioned C.P.C.s and found that there were only about
1600 with a shortage of 700 and more.

It is suspected that the above 2 shops might
have concerned together and intended to misappropriate
the cheap rice for a better price.

This suspected practice may be carried out
by other shops dealing with cheap rice.

I am, Sir,

Your obedient servant,
Shao Kwang Liang
Sub Inspector.

报告

事由：关于浙江路690号及厦门路84号米店出售平价米事宜之观察。

呈报人：副巡长邵光亮（Shao Kwang Liang）。由老闸捕房主管警官转呈。

归档
1940年10月21日

先生：

谨此报告，1940年10月5日下午1时至5时之间，卑职会同华籍警长（C.P.C.）第77、79及427号，在浙江路690号及厦门路84号米店执勤，监管这两家店铺的平价米销售情况。

1940年10月5日下午1时，上述前一家店铺开始发售凭券，持该券可向后一家店铺领取大米。据悉，每日计划发售粮票2400张。

下午约2时30分，前一家店铺宣布粮票已售罄。卑职对此声明表示怀疑，因为此项工作理应需要更长的时间。

下午约4时30分，后一家店铺停止发米，此后未见有人前来领米。随后，卑职在上述华籍警长的协助下，核对了回收的粮票数量，发现仅有约1600张，短缺700余张。

怀疑上述两家店铺可能串通一气，意图侵吞平价米以高价牟利。

其他经营平价米的店铺也可能存在此类可疑行为。

此致，

您顺从的仆人，
邵光亮
副巡长。

Translation of letter to Chinese
Deputy Secretary from Shanghai Rice
Cheap Sale Committee.

Dated 21st September, 1940.

Rice Cheap sales: Police protection wanted.

We have continued the cheap sale of rice daily from
2 p.m. (D.S.T.) since the 19th instant. Although the
Police Department was requested in advance to accord us
protection, according to telephone messages received from
various rice shops, constables either failed to arrive
in time or did not turn up at all yesterday; the result
was that there was some disorder and in some cases shop
counters and furniture were destroyed by the overwhelming
crowd of purchasers. During the previous cheap sale period
the price of rice was not so high as now, so that
purchasers were comparatively few and police protection
was not very urgent. As we cannot dispense with police
protection for a moment at the present time, will you
please request the Police Authorities to send Constables
to the shops punctually to ensure safety. Attention
should be given particularly to shops under the jurisdiction
of the Gordon Road and Pootoo Road Police Stations. Please
give this matter attention and oblige.

(Chopped) Yu Ya-ch'ing
Chairman.
Address: No.95, Canton Road
Tel. No.13674.

(Note: Received for translation a.m. 23rd September, 1940.)

日期：1940年9月21日。

平价米销售：请求警务保护。

自本月19日起，我们每天下午2时（夏令时）继续平价售米。虽然事先已请求警务部门给予保护，但根据各家米店收到的电话消息，昨日巡捕要么未能及时赶到，要么根本未到；结果导致现场出现一些混乱，在某些情况下，柜台和家具被 overwhelming 的购买人群毁坏。在之前的平价销售期间，米价不像现在这么高，因此购买者相对较少，警务保护的需求也不那么迫切。鉴于目前我们片刻也离不开警务保护，恳请贵方要求警务当局准时派遣巡捕前往各店铺，以确保安全。请特别关注戈登路（Gordon Road）和普陀路（Pootoo Road）捕房辖区内的店铺。请对此事予以关注，不胜感激。

（盖章）虞洽卿
主席。

电话：13674。

Translation of letter to Council
from the Shanghai Committee for
Cheap sale of Rice.

Dated 12th September, 1940.

Rice: Cheap sales.

More than eight months have passed since this Committee
was formed on 5th January this year. We are very grateful to
the Council for according us sympathetic support and to the
various business Associations and individuals for their generous
contributions and assistance. To sell rice at cheap price to
relieve the poor is in accord with our natural duty to help
our fellow-beings. In the past, such sales have always been
conducted as temporary expedients and have never been continued
for any protracted time. The members of our Committee tremble
constantly in view of their heavy responsibility. In the first
period cheap sales were held on three occasions. A total of
102,696 bags of Saigon rice was sold at a loss of more than
$718,400.

During the second period cheap sales were conducted twice.
As about 20,000 bags were sold, we suffered a loss of over
$187,000. Up to the present we have still over 34,000 bags,
which are barely sufficient for two months. Since we have
exhausted our means in connexion with the raising of funds for
the purchase of rice, we now propose to wind up our work as
soon as the remaining stock is sold out. As we must notify the
public in advance, the Council is hereby requested to take note
and oblige.

(Signed) Yu Ya-ching
Chairman

（批：Acknowledged by Secretariat.）

上海平价米销售委员会致工部局信函译文。

日期：1940年9月12日。

大米：平价销售。

本委员会自今年1月5日成立以来，已逾八个多月。我们非常感谢工部局给予我们的同情支持，以及各商业团体和个人慷慨的捐助与协助。以低价售米救济贫民，符合我们要帮助同胞的天职。过去，此类销售一直作为临时权宜之计进行，从未长期持续。本委员会成员鉴于责任重大，始终战战兢兢。在第一阶段，共举行了三次平价销售。总计售出西贡米102,696袋，亏损超过718,400元。

在第二阶段，进行了两次平价销售。由于售出约20,000袋，我们亏损超过187,000元。截至目前，我们仍存有34,000余袋，仅够维持两个月。由于我们在筹集购米资金方面已耗尽手段，现提议在剩余库存售完后尽快结束我们的工作。由于我们必须提前通知公众，特此请求工部局知悉，不胜感激。

（签名）虞洽卿
主席

addressed to the Council from the Shanghai Rice

The Shanghai Municipal Council:

In compliance with the request of the
Shanghai Rice Cheap Sales Committee we have decided to
sell rice at reduced prices for the sixth period from
2 p.m. (Day Light Saving Time) on September 19th.
Sixty rice shops have been entrusted to sell rice
tickets and to distribute rice: 36 in the International
Settlement (18 for selling rice tickets and 18 for
distributing rice) and 24 in the French Concession (12
for selling rice tickets and 12 for distributing rice).
Herewith we submit 30 copies of a table
showing the names and addresses of those shops above
referred to. It is requested that the various Police
Stations be instructed to duly detail policemen to the
various places where the sale of rice tickets and the
distribution of rice will take place in due course.

Shanghai Rice Shops' Association
(Chopped)

addresses of rice shops.

September 17, 1940.

The Shanghai Cheap Rice Sales Committee
will re-commence sales at rice shops in the
Settlement and French Concession from September 19,
1940. The hours of sale will be from 2 p.m. to
5 p.m. daily. A number of shops will sell coupons
entitling the holder to purchase 4 Shih Chin (catties)
of rice for $1.00. The coupon will bear the
address of the shop at which the rice may be
purchased.

Purchasers are hereby called upon to
take note that as the sales are conducted as a
philanthropic undertaking intended to benefit
the people they must observe strict order and
not cause any disturbance while making their
purchases. Should unruly characters create
any trouble at these rice shops on any pretext
whatsoever, they will be instantly arrested and
severely punished.

Shops selling coupons and rice are
listed in all newspapers.

By order
Commissioner of Police.

一九四〇年九月十七日。

上海平价米销售委员会将于一九四〇年九月十九日起，在公共租界及法租界的米店恢复销售。每日销售时间为下午二时至五时。部分米店将出售购米券，持券人可凭券以一元购买四市斤大米。购米券上将印有可凭此购买大米的米店地址。

特此告诫购买者注意，鉴于此次销售系为造福民众之慈善性质活动，购买时必须严守秩序，不得在购买过程中引发任何骚乱。若有不法之徒以任何借口在上述米店滋事，将立即予以逮捕并严惩不贷。

be held at 3 p.m. August 10 to discuss arrangements for

July 11, 1940.

To the S.M.C.

At the request of the Rice Cheap Sales
Committee, this guild will undertake the fourth cheap
sale of rice. We have appointed 30 shops to sell
coupons and 30 shops issue rice. 36 of the shops
are located in the International Settlement 18 of
which will sell coupons while the remaining 18 shops
will issue rice. 24 shops are located in the French
Concession; 12 shops to sell coupons and the remaining
12 to issue rice.

Owing to the hot weather, the sales and issues
will be conducted between 7 a.m. and 10 a.m. (Summer
Time). The transportation and delivery of the rice to
shops will be carried out after 12 noon each day.

30 copies of a list of the rice shops
designated by this guild are attached for your reference,
and for the information of the police stations concerned.

Please instruct the Police stations to
appoint policemen for duty at the shops to maintain order.
The policemen on duty should pay particular attention to
the arrival of trucks with rice for cheap sale on every
afternoon. Cases happened in the past wherein policemen
detained trucks loaded with 50 bags each on the ground
that they were overloaded. As the Cheap Sales Committee
stipulates that each place has to sell 50 bags a day,
it is necessary that one truck should carry this quantity.
Please instruct the Police not to interfere in such cases
so as to facilitate the sale.

(Signed) Shanghai Rice Shop Owners'
Guild.

July 12, 1940.

The Shanghai Committee for Cheap Sale of
Rice will re-commence sales at rice shops in the
Settlement and French Concession, from July 16,
1940. The hours of sale will be from 7 a.m. to
10 a.m. daily. A number of shops will sell
coupons entitling the holder to purchase 4
Shih Chin (catties) of rice for $1.00. The
coupon will bear the address of the shop at
which the rice may be purchased.

Purchasers are hereby called upon to
take note that as the sales are conducted as
a philanthropic undertaking intended to benefit
the people they must observe strict order and
not cause any disturbance while making their
purchases. Should unruly characters create any
trouble at these rice shops on any pretext
whatsoever, they will be instantly arrested and
severely punished.

Shops selling coupons and rice are listed
in all newspapers.

By order

Commissioner of Police.

1940年7月12日。

上海平价米销售委员会将于1940年7月16日起，在租界及法租界的米店恢复销售。销售时间为每日上午7时至10时。部分米店将出售购米证，持证人可凭此以1.00元购买4市斤大米。购米证上将印有可购买大米的米店地址。

特此呼吁购买者注意，鉴于此次销售旨在造福民众的慈善性质，大家在购买时必须严格遵守秩序，不得制造任何骚乱。若有不法之徒以任何借口在这些米店制造麻烦，将立即逮捕并严惩。

出售购米证和大米的米店名单已在所有报纸上刊登。

奉命

警务处处长。

Fourteen members of the Shanghai Cheap Rice
Sales Committee held a meeting in the Shanghai
Navigation Club, 93 Canton Road, between 4 p.m. and 5.30
p.m. July 2 with Mr. Yu Ya Ching presiding. The
following resolutions were discussed and passed :-
1. That cheap sales of rice be conducted as from
July 16, 1940, and that sixty rice shops in the
Settlement and French Concession be requested to
carry out the sales (30 shops to sell coupons and
30 shops to issue rice.)
2. That the sales be started with the 15,000 bags
of rice on hand which were left over from the
previous sales and that the sales be temporarily
suspended should it be found that the rice on
order will not arrive in time to carry on with
the sales.
3. That each purchaser will be allowed to buy not
more than $1 worth of rice at $40.00 per "zar",
i.e. $1 for 4 catties.
4. That a total of 1,500 bags of rice be disposed off
in one day at 50 bags each shop.
5. That the sales be carried out in the forenoon
instead of in the afternoon as on previous occasions,
because of the hot weather, and that definite hours
be decided upon by the Shanghai Rice Shop Owners'
Guild.
